log.notes_to_self: Day 1: killed 9, omitting both hospital cases. Baseline strategy: kill national plus all South/radio/forum/foreign cases (9/day), omit hospital. Put EVERY death in afternoon using quick entries (up to 10); this preserves students, night workers and home routines, totaling 55% of population. Morning deaths could unnecessarily eliminate students. Timed entries offer no benefit for this schedule. Nine daily kills produce double scoring on day 4 and quadruple from day 5, totaling 981 if maintained uncaught. We intentionally accept some early detection risk to obtain much higher expected scoring than a permanently low-volume strategy. Omitting sector leaves the largest suspect cushion: if hospital is reachable (prior 60%), only two of our four nonnational source kinds are reachable, so even full disclosure leaves at least 3437 suspects indefinitely. If hospital is inaccessible (40%), three used kinds are reachable and discovery of all three risks capture. Do not casually add hospital kills: that can destroy an otherwise permanently safe configuration. All three reachable kinds fully learned would fall below 1000 with our routine restriction. Press conferences every 3 days are the only trace feedback; we do NOT know which deaths were traced. Approximate pools absent cross-report ambiguity: routine only 55000 (announced 60000); one nonsector dimension 13750 (10000); two 3438 (3000). Hidden second reports can soften constraints or prevent traces. Remember the objective is expected points, not survival alone; reassess using announcements, but do not abandon high throughput merely because the pool has safely stabilized around 3000.
